verdict.delta_sentence: Compared with the nearer intent-classification-2 reference, this board has similarly clear color-coded sections but uses the frame far less effectively and exposes substantially more awkward branching and retry-routing machinery.

sub_checks.name: frame_use
sub_checks.note: Failure: the workflow is packed into the upper-left while roughly half the frame remains empty across the right and bottom, creating severe visual imbalance.

sub_checks.name: corridors_and_air
sub_checks.note: Most nodes and labels have generous breathing room, although several branch corridors in the lower blue and central orange sections tighten into visually busy junctions.

sub_checks.name: grouping
sub_checks.note: The three softly tinted, titled phase regions provide clear and useful grouping, with node colors reinforcing roles across region boundaries.

sub_checks.name: color
sub_checks.note: Blue, orange, green, yellow, and red are applied consistently enough to convey phase and status, though the mixed role-versus-phase semantics require some inference.

sub_checks.name: machinery_leakage
sub_checks.note: Failure: exposed T-junction stubs, arrowheads aimed at shared rails, and the central retry loop make routing construction visibly intrude on the diagram.

sub_checks.name: alignment_and_rhythm
sub_checks.note: Vertical stacks and section headers hold strong registers, but the dense first two phases beside the sparse third phase and vast unused frame produce an uneven overall rhythm.

sub_checks.name: edge_legibility
sub_checks.note: Failure: primary vertical sequences are clear, but the central parallel branches, return loop, and lower decision splits contain ambiguous rail merges and awkward terminal geometry.

verdict.rank_order_sanity_note: The assigned scores and visual ordering agree: gc-decomp-harness ranks first, intent-classification-2 second, and the board under grade third.
